ch26.sub: The Emergency Son of Salem and the Covenant of Faith
ch26.sum: For thousands of years after the failure of the Adamic mission, revealed truth was in danger of dying out. Then Machiventa Melchizedek, one of the planetary receivers, volunteered to appear in human form at Salem. He taught one God, the Father of all, and made a covenant with Abraham that the favor of God is had not by sacrifices and burnt offerings but by faith. His teachings spread east and west through missionaries, though they were often swallowed up by older superstitions. This chapter considers in turn the bestowal of the emergency Son, the teaching and creed of Salem, the covenant with Abraham, and the legacy by which Melchizedek prepared the way for Michael's bestowal. The gospel that salvation is a gift received by faith was proclaimed on this earth nearly two thousand years before Jesus.
ch26.s1: The Bestowal of an Emergency Son
ch26.s1.u1.k: The Melchizedeks are the emergency Sons who step in when extraordinary problems arise.
ch26.s1.u1.p: To understand Machiventa's story we must first know the order to which he belongs. The Melchizedek Sons are the most versatile beings of a local universe; they can work not only on spirit levels but even on the level of material personality manifestation. So when established plans break down and the unexpected arises, they willingly take up the burden. A world like Urantia, wounded by rebellion and default, needed exactly such a Son.

text: THE Melchizedeks are widely known as emergency Sons, for they engage in an amazing range of activities on the worlds of a local universe. When any extraordinary problem arises, or when something unusual is to be attempted, it is quite often a Melchizedek who accepts the assignment. The ability of the Melchizedek Sons to function in emergencies and on widely divergent levels of the universe, even on the physical level of personality manifestation, is peculiar to their order.

ch26.s1.u2.k: When truth was dying out, Machiventa volunteered to become a man and bestow himself on the world.
ch26.s1.u2.p: Mankind was advancing intellectually while slipping backward spiritually. The higher authorities told the planetary receivers to find their own way, and Machiventa's offer of himself was the answer. Because he took up out of love a task no one had ordered, this bestowal already resembles the bestowal of Michael that was to come.

text: Revealed truth was threatened with extinction during the millenniums which followed the miscarriage of the Adamic mission on Urantia. Though making progress intellectually, the human races were slowly losing ground spiritually. About 3000 B.C. the concept of God had grown very hazy in the minds of men.

And it was in consequence of having been thrown so completely on their own resources that Machiventa Melchizedek, one of the twelve planetary receivers, volunteered to do that which had been done only six times in all the history of Nebadon: to personalize on earth as a temporary man of the realm, to bestow himself as an emergency Son of world ministry.

ch26.s1.u3.k: Machiventa appeared quietly as priest of the one God, and a Thought Adjuster indwelt him.
ch26.s1.u3.p: His coming carried no spectacular signs. A brief statement to a herdsman in his tent, that he was priest of the Most High, was the whole proclamation of his mission. More remarkable still, a Thought Adjuster dwelt within him, and through this experience that Adjuster was prepared to work later in the mind of Michael incarnate. From the start, Melchizedek's bestowal pointed toward the life of Jesus.

text: His coming was unspectacular; his materialization was not witnessed by human eyes. He was first observed by mortal man on that eventful day when he entered the tent of Amdon, a Chaldean herder of Sumerian extraction. And the proclamation of his mission was embodied in the simple statement which he made to this shepherd, "I am Melchizedek, priest of El Elyon, the Most High, the one and only God."

This incarnated Melchizedek received a Thought Adjuster, who indwelt his superhuman personality as the monitor of time and the mentor of the flesh, thus gaining that experience and practical introduction to Urantian problems and to the technique of indwelling an incarnated Son which enabled this spirit of the Father to function so valiantly in the human mind of the later Son of God, Michael, when he appeared on earth in the likeness of mortal flesh.

ch26.s2.u1.k: Melchizedek subordinated all his teaching to the doctrine of one God, a divine Father.
ch26.s2.u1.p: The teacher of Salem taught only as much as his pupils could receive. But the center of all his teaching was always one God, not a distant tribal deity but the heavenly Creator and Father. The emphasis had a clear aim: to awaken man's adoration and to prepare the road for the coming of a Son of that same Father.

text: Melchizedek taught his followers all they had capacity to receive and assimilate. … But this great teacher subordinated everything to the doctrine of one God, a universe Deity, a heavenly Creator, a divine Father. Emphasis was placed upon this teaching for the purpose of appealing to man's adoration and of preparing the way for the subsequent appearance of Michael as the Son of this same Universal Father.

ch26.s2.u2.k: The Salem creed was brief, yet its teaching of favor by faith was far ahead of its time.
ch26.s2.u2.p: A creed of only three articles holds the heart of theology: believe in the one Father, accept the covenant that grants favor to faith rather than to offerings, and tell this good news to all men. Yet people could not grasp receiving divine favor for nothing. The ancient belief that man is born in debt to the gods stood in the way of that idea.

text: 1. I believe in El Elyon, the Most High God, the only Universal Father and Creator of all things.
2. I accept the Melchizedek covenant with the Most High, which bestows the favor of God on my faith, not on sacrifices and burnt offerings.
3. I promise to obey the seven commandments of Melchizedek and to tell the good news of this covenant with the Most High to all men.

And that was the whole of the creed of the Salem colony. But even such a short and simple declaration of faith was altogether too much and too advanced for the men of those days. They simply could not grasp the idea of getting divine favor for nothing—by faith. They were too deeply confirmed in the belief that man was born under forfeit to the gods.

ch26.s2.u3.k: Melchizedek offered a sacrament of bread and wine in place of blood sacrifice, to change old customs gradually.
ch26.s2.u3.p: Customs are not changed overnight by a single truth. Knowing this, Melchizedek forbade sacrifice but did not leave its place empty; he put bread and wine there instead. Yet even Abraham fell back on the old sacrifice after his victory. The passage honestly shows that however clear revelation may be, the human heart tends to return to the familiar.

text: While no sacrifices were permitted within the colony, Melchizedek well knew how difficult it is to suddenly uproot long-established customs and accordingly had wisely offered these people the substitute of a sacrament of bread and wine for the older sacrifice of flesh and blood. … Even Abraham resorted to this barbarous practice after his victory over Chedorlaomer; he simply did not feel quite at ease until he had offered a conventional sacrifice.

ch26.s3.u1.k: Abraham gave up the dream of material conquest for the spiritual concept of the kingdom of heaven.
ch26.s3.u1.p: To speak of a "chosen people" can mislead, but it is right to call Abraham a chosen individual. He was an ambitious man who meant to conquer all Canaan. Melchizedek did not so much crush that ambition as turn it toward a greater goal: a kingdom built by the spirit instead of the sword. One man's change of direction opened the spiritual history of a people.

text: Although it may be an error to speak of "chosen people," it is not a mistake to refer to Abraham as a chosen individual. Melchizedek did lay upon Abraham the responsibility of keeping alive the truth of one God as distinguished from the prevailing belief in plural deities.

Abraham envisaged the conquest of all Canaan. … He arranged another conference with Melchizedek; and it was in the course of this interview that the priest of Salem, the visible Son of God, persuaded Abraham to abandon his scheme of material conquest and temporal rule in favor of the spiritual concept of the kingdom of heaven.

ch26.s3.u2.k: In Melchizedek's covenant God agrees to do everything; man agrees only to believe his promises.
ch26.s3.u2.p: This covenant changed the relation between God and man from bargain to trust. Until then salvation had to be bought by works of sacrifice and offering; now favor became a gift received by faith. The ancient words that Abraham believed and it was counted to him for righteousness point to this very shift.

text: And Melchizedek made a formal covenant with Abraham at Salem. Said he to Abraham: "Look now up to the heavens and number the stars if you are able; so numerous shall your seed be." And Abraham believed Melchizedek, "and it was counted to him for righteousness."

This covenant of Melchizedek with Abraham represents the great Urantian agreement between divinity and humanity whereby God agrees to do everything; man only agrees to believe God's promises and follow his instructions. Heretofore it had been believed that salvation could be secured only by works—sacrifices and offerings; now, Melchizedek again brought to Urantia the good news that salvation, favor with God, is to be had by faith.

ch26.s4.u1.k: The Salem missionaries carried the gospel of faith and trust across the Eastern Hemisphere.
ch26.s4.u1.p: Melchizedek's teaching did not stay in Salem. The early teachers of the Salem religion went to distant tribes of Africa and Eurasia with the same message: the only price of divine favor is faith and trust. They worked by training local converts to become teachers in turn. Revelation begins with one person but spreads through the devotion of many.

text: THE early teachers of the Salem religion penetrated to the remotest tribes of Africa and Eurasia, ever preaching Machiventa's gospel of man's faith and trust in the one universal God as the only price of obtaining divine favor. … They established training centers in different parts of the world where they taught the natives the Salem religion and then commissioned these pupils to function as teachers among their own people.

ch26.s4.u2.k: A new revelation is always prone to be blurred by older evolutionary beliefs.
ch26.s4.u2.p: The gospel of Salem spread widely but did not long stay pure. New teaching always tended to be absorbed into old ritual and magic. Still the spark never went fully out; in Europe those who preached faith and trust in God survived into the Christian era and joined the new religion. Truth may be dimmed, but it does not disappear.

text: There was always a tendency for the new doctrine to become absorbed into the older body of religious teaching and magical practice. A new revelation is always contaminated by the older evolutionary beliefs.

For a long time in Europe the Salem missionaries carried on their activities, becoming gradually absorbed into many of the cults and ritual groups which periodically arose. … These preachers of faith and trust in God were still functioning in Roman Europe in the first century after Christ, being later incorporated into the newly forming Christian religion.

ch26.s4.u3.k: Melchizedek came to keep alive the truth of one God and to prepare for a Paradise Son's bestowal.
ch26.s4.u3.p: Melchizedek did not try to reform moral codes or daily habits. His work was plainly twofold: to keep the truth of one God from dying out on earth, and to prepare the way for the Father's Son to come as a man. When Michael came, he confirmed everything Melchizedek had taught about the Father. The faith of Salem and the gospel of Galilee form a single stream.

text: Like Jesus, Melchizedek attended strictly to the fulfillment of the mission of his bestowal. He did not attempt to reform the mores, to change the habits of the world, nor to promulgate even advanced sanitary practices or scientific truths. He came to achieve two tasks: to keep alive on earth the truth of the one God and to prepare the way for the subsequent mortal bestowal of a Paradise Son of that Universal Father.
And Michael, when he appeared on earth, confirmed all that Melchizedek had taught concerning the Paradise Father.

ch26.s4.u4.k: Machiventa still serves this planet as a representative of Christ Michael.
ch26.s4.u4.p: The sage of Salem vanished, but his service did not end. He remained a planetary receiver until Michael's triumph and now bears the title Vicegerent Planetary Prince of Urantia. That a Son who once walked this earth in human form still labors for this world reminds us that our planet has never been abandoned.

text: Machiventa continued as a planetary receiver up to the times of the triumph of Michael on Urantia. Subsequently, he was attached to the Urantia service on Jerusem as one of the four and twenty directors, only just recently having been elevated to the position of personal ambassador on Jerusem of the Creator Son, bearing the title Vicegerent Planetary Prince of Urantia.

ch26.qs1: Are there times when I too find it hard to accept that God's favor is freely received by faith? Why might that be?
ch26.qs2: Where in my life might I, like Abraham, need to turn my ambitions toward a greater spiritual purpose?
ch26.qs3: When I meet a new truth, how do I deal with the pull to fall back on familiar old habits?
ch27.sub: The Evolution of the Hebrew Concept of God
ch27.sum: The Hebrew concept of God was not handed down complete from the beginning. Yahweh, the god of desert tribes associated with the volcano of Sinai, became through Moses the Lord God of Israel, and in the preaching of Samuel, Amos, Hosea, and Micah grew into a God who is changeless, just, and merciful. Jeremiah proclaimed him the God of all nations, and Isaiah of the captivity portrayed the all-powerful Creator as the all-loving Father. Remarkably, through all these changes the name remained Yahweh. This chapter considers in turn how God-concepts grow, the compromise and limits of Moses, the contribution of the prophets, and the final steps toward the Universal Father. This history shows how revelation unfolds gradually within human understanding.
ch27.s1: How the Concept of God Grows
ch27.s1.u1.k: Man first includes all gods, then subordinates them, and finally excludes all but the one God.
ch27.s1.u1.p: The history of God-concepts usually passes through three stages: first all gods are accepted, then foreign gods are placed beneath one's own tribal god, and at last only the One of supreme value remains. The Hebrews walked this road, but not in a straight line. From polytheism through henotheism to monotheism they slipped backward many times, and even in a single age different groups thought of God differently.

text: IN CONCEIVING of Deity, man first includes all gods, then subordinates all foreign gods to his tribal deity, and finally excludes all but the one God of final and supreme value. The Jews synthesized all gods into their more sublime concept of the Lord God of Israel.

The progress of the Hebrews from polytheism through henotheism to monotheism was not an unbroken and continuous conceptual development. They experienced many retrogressions in the evolution of their Deity concepts, while during any one epoch there existed varying ideas of God among different groups of Semite believers.

ch27.s1.u2.k: The Hebrews changed their concept of God but never changed his name, Yahweh.
ch27.s1.u2.p: The idea of Yahweh underwent the widest development of any human theory of God. From the tribal god of Mount Horeb to the loving and merciful Creator Father, its content changed almost to its opposite, yet the name stayed the same. Under a single name in the Scriptures, then, lie layer upon layer of understandings from different ages. Knowing this lets us read the rougher expressions of the old records with patience.

text: The idea of Yahweh has undergone the most extensive development of all the mortal theories of God. … But as a matter of historic fact, it should be understood that, while the Jews thus changed their views of Deity from the tribal god of Mount Horeb to the loving and merciful Creator Father of later times, they did not change his name; they continued all the way along to call this evolving concept of Deity, Yahweh.

ch27.s2: Moses and the Yahweh of Sinai
ch27.s2.u1.k: Moses borrowed the name of the desert tribal god Yahweh to teach a higher God.
ch27.s2.u1.p: Moses knew El Elyon, the Most High God, but he also knew that a people just out of slavery could not grasp that teaching. So he adopted Yahweh, the desert god they already knew, and tried to pour a higher God into that name. It was a deliberate compromise suited to the people's level. Even lofty truth must be poured into a vessel the hearers can receive.

text: Moses had endeavored to teach these Bedouins the idea of El Elyon, but before leaving Egypt, he had become convinced they would never fully comprehend this doctrine. Therefore he deliberately determined upon the compromise adoption of their tribal god of the desert as the one and only god of his followers.

ch27.s2.u2.k: Despite Moses' lofty teaching, the people's concept of God stayed primitive and anthropomorphic.
ch27.s2.u2.p: Moses labored to exalt Yahweh as a God of truth without iniquity. But to meet his hearers where they were, God was pictured as one who grows angry, takes vengeance, and is easily swayed by human conduct. When Moses was gone, the people soon slid back to their older ideas. It takes long ages for one leader's insight to become a people's understanding.

text: Moses made a heroic effort to uplift Yahweh to the dignity of a supreme Deity when he presented him as the "God of truth and without iniquity, just and right in all his ways." And yet, despite this exalted teaching, the limited understanding of his followers made it necessary to speak of God as being in man's image, as being subject to fits of anger, wrath, and severity, even that he was vengeful and easily influenced by man's conduct.

While Moses presented fleeting glimpses of a universal and beneficent Deity to the children of Israel, on the whole, their day-by-day concept of Yahweh was that of a God but little better than the tribal gods of the surrounding peoples. Their concept of God was primitive, crude, and anthropomorphic; when Moses passed on, these Bedouin tribes quickly reverted to the semibarbaric ideas of their olden gods of Horeb and the desert.

ch27.s3.u1.k: Samuel proclaimed Yahweh to be a changeless God of perfection.
ch27.s3.u1.p: People of that time thought of Yahweh as a fitful god who was forever regretting what he had done. Samuel drew a firm line against this: God is not a man, so he neither lies nor changes his mind. The declaration gave faith a stable foundation. Trust can grow only where there is assurance that God stands firm even when human hearts waver.

text: In these times Yahweh was conceived to be a fitful God of jealous whims, always regretting that he had done thus and so; but now, for the first time since the Hebrews sallied forth from Egypt, they heard these startling words, "The Strength of Israel will not lie nor repent, for he is not a man, that he should repent." Stability in dealing with Divinity was proclaimed.

ch27.s3.u2.k: Amos proclaimed Yahweh the God of all nations, who would not condone sin even in his own people.
ch27.s3.u2.p: A tribal god who can be appeased by sacrifice and ceremony will overlook the wrongs of his own people. Amos attacked exactly that notion. Being a chosen people does not excuse crime and oppression, and ritual cannot replace righteousness. He was stoned to death, but the leaven of truth he left behind kept alive the doctrine of the supreme Yahweh.

text: A great step in the transition of the tribal god—the god who had so long been served with sacrifices and ceremonies, the Yahweh of the earlier Hebrews—to a God who would punish crime and immorality among even his own people, was taken by Amos, who appeared from among the southern hills to denounce the criminality, drunkenness, oppression, and immorality of the northern tribes.

Amos proclaimed Yahweh the "God of all nations" and warned the Israelites that ritual must not take the place of righteousness. And before this courageous teacher was stoned to death, he had spread enough leaven of truth to save the doctrine of the supreme Yahweh; he had insured the further evolution of the Melchizedek revelation.

ch27.s3.u3.k: Hosea preached forgiveness through repentance, not sacrifice, and the mercy of God.
ch27.s3.u3.p: If Amos cried out for justice, Hosea sang of love. He preached forgiveness through repentance, not sacrifice, saying that God loves his people faithfully, as in a marriage covenant. Justice and mercy do not quarrel. Because Amos awakened conscience and Hosea struck the first notes of mercy, Isaiah after them could complete the chord.

text: Hosea preached forgiveness through repentance, not by sacrifice. He proclaimed a gospel of loving-kindness and divine mercy, saying: "I will betroth you to me forever; yes, I will betroth you to me in righteousness and judgment and in loving-kindness and in mercies. I will even betroth you to me in faithfulness."

Amos quickened the national conscience of the Hebrews to the recognition that Yahweh would not condone crime and sin among them because they were supposedly the chosen people, while Hosea struck the opening notes in the later merciful chords of divine compassion and loving-kindness which were so exquisitely sung by Isaiah and his associates.

ch27.s3.u4.k: Micah declared that God requires not offerings but justice, mercy, and a humble walk with him.
ch27.s3.u4.p: Neither burnt offerings, nor a thousand rams, nor ten thousand rivers of oil can please God. Micah's question shook the whole system of blood offerings to its roots. What God asks of man is to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with him. This brief question and answer holds the heart of prophetic faith, and it remains just as valid for believers today.

text: Ever the burden of Micah's message was: "Shall I come before God with burnt offerings? Will the Lord be pleased with a thousand rams or with ten thousand rivers of oil? … He has shown me, O man, what is good; and what does the Lord require of you but to do justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God?"

ch27.s4.u1.k: Jeremiah proclaimed that Yahweh took no side with the Hebrews but was God of all the earth.
ch27.s4.u1.p: A god who takes our side in war is in the end only an enlargement of our own nation. Jeremiah was branded a traitor for saying that Yahweh did not side with the Hebrews in their military struggles. Yet because of that courage, the God of Israel crossed the boundaries of the nation. Yahweh is the God of all nations and all peoples, the God of all the earth.

text: Jeremiah fearlessly declared that Yahweh was not on the side of the Hebrews in their military struggles with other nations. He asserted that Yahweh was God of all the earth, of all nations and of all peoples.

ch27.s4.u2.k: The captivity liberated the Yahweh concept, and the second Isaiah reached the highest concept of God.
ch27.s4.u2.p: The pain of losing their nation actually enlarged their concept of God. In Babylon, with neither temple nor land, the Hebrews learned that Yahweh was not bound to one place or one people. In that season the second Isaiah proclaimed no small man-made god, but a God who takes up the isles as a very little thing and whose thoughts are higher than ours.

text: The later captivity that enslaved the Jews in Babylon finally liberated the evolving concept of Yahweh to assume the monotheistic role of the God of all nations.

No prophet or religious teacher from Machiventa to the time of Jesus attained the high concept of God that Isaiah the second proclaimed during these days of the captivity. It was no small, anthropomorphic, man-made God that this spiritual leader proclaimed. "Behold he takes up the isles as a very little thing." "And as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways and my thoughts higher than your thoughts."

ch27.s4.u3.k: The Hebrew prophets deanthropomorphized God without making him an abstraction; he remained a Father.
ch27.s4.u3.p: Strip God of human form and what often remains is a principle only philosophers can understand. The achievement of the Hebrew spiritual leaders lay in avoiding that trap. Isaiah eclipsed the nationalistic Yahweh with his sublime portrait of the God of love, ruler of the universe, and Father of all mankind, and he portrayed the almighty Creator as the all-loving Father.

text: The farseeing and courageous Isaiah effectively eclipsed the nationalistic Yahweh by his sublime portraiture of the majesty and universal omnipotence of the supreme Yahweh, God of love, ruler of the universe, and affectionate Father of all mankind. … In superb language and with matchless grace this great teacher portrayed the all-powerful Creator as the all-loving Father.

THE spiritual leaders of the Hebrews did what no others before them had ever succeeded in doing—they deanthropomorphized their God concept without converting it into an abstraction of Deity comprehensible only to philosophers. Even common people were able to regard the matured concept of Yahweh as a Father, if not of the individual, at least of the race.

ch27.s4.u4.k: Jesus taught his apostles how the God idea grew from Yahweh to the Father in heaven.
ch27.s4.u4.p: Jesus did not hide the history of the Hebrew concept of God; he taught it to his apostles plainly. Without being ashamed of its crude beginnings, he showed that its end is the Father in heaven. Especially worth noting is his word that God never rejects sincere worship, whatever the name or concept by which he is addressed. Concepts of God grow, but the Father's acceptance has been constant from the start.

text: 1. Yahweh—the god of the Sinai clans. This was the primitive concept of Deity which Moses exalted to the higher level of the Lord God of Israel. The Father in heaven never fails to accept the sincere worship of his children on earth, no matter how crude their concept of Deity or by what name they symbolize his divine nature.

6. The Father in heaven. And now do we know God as our Father in heaven. … At all times and during all ages the true worship of any human being—as concerns individual spiritual progress—is recognized by the indwelling spirit as homage rendered to the Father in heaven.

ch27.qs1: How has my concept of God grown from childhood until now? What traces of a 'tribal god' still remain?
ch27.qs2: What does Micah's call to do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly mean in my life today?
ch27.qs3: When I meet people who worship God under another name and concept, what attitude does the history in this chapter ask of me?
ch28.sub: The Father's Eternal Purpose and Salvation by Faith
ch28.sum: In the Urantia Book salvation is not a bargain for appeasing an angry God; it is a gift set within the eternal plan of the Deities to raise the creatures of time to the perfection of eternity. The Father's plan of attainment, the Son's bestowal plan, and the Infinite Spirit's plan of mercy ministry together achieve this purpose. The bestowals of the Sons are not meant to change the Father's attitude, and the death on the cross was no offering to appease wrath. Salvation is the Father's gift received by faith, and the righteous life is not its condition but its fruit. This chapter considers in turn the structure of the divine plan, the error of atonement ideas, sonship by faith, and the salvation of forgiveness and love. God is a Father before he is a judge, and his love does not merely set sin aside but renews a person and leads him to eternal survival.
ch28.s1: The Divine Plan of Perfection Attainment
ch28.s1.u1.k: Salvation begins in the joint plan of Father and Son to lead the beings of time to eternal perfection.
ch28.s1.u1.p: To see salvation only as the solution to the problem of sin is to see just one corner of the picture. The Urantia Book sets salvation within a far larger frame. Father and Son are one in a vast plan to raise material beings to eternal perfection. Its starting point is the plan of progressive attainment, which includes the bestowal of Thought Adjusters and the gift of personality. Salvation is not damage control; it is a purpose intended from the beginning.

text: The Father and his Son are as one in the formulation and prosecution of this gigantic attainment plan for advancing the material beings of time to the perfection of eternity. This project for the spiritual elevation of the ascendant souls of space is a joint creation of the Father and the Son, and they are, with the co-operation of the Infinite Spirit, engaged in associative execution of their divine purpose.

1. The Plan of Progressive Attainment. This is the Universal Father's plan of evolutionary ascension, a program unreservedly accepted by the Eternal Son when he concurred in the Father's proposal, "Let us make mortal creatures in our own image." This provision for upstepping the creatures of time involves the Father's bestowal of the Thought Adjusters and the endowing of material creatures with the prerogatives of personality.

ch28.s1.u2.k: The Deities together foster the plan of ascension and, if required, co-operate in restoration and rehabilitation.
ch28.s1.u2.p: Having proclaimed the universal mandate to be perfect, the Father intrusted the execution of that tremendous undertaking to the Eternal Son, who fosters it together with the Infinite Spirit. Where rebellion mars the plan, the bestowals of the Sons recover what was lost, and to this is added the mercy ministry of the Infinite Spirit. Because the plans of the three Deities interlock, no world lies outside the reach of restoration.

text: Having promulgated the universal mandate, "Be you perfect, even as I am perfect," the Father intrusted the execution of this tremendous undertaking to the Eternal Son; and the Eternal Son shares the fostering of this supernal enterprise with his divine co-ordinate, the Infinite Spirit. Thus do the Deities effectively co-operate in the work of creation, control, evolution, revelation, and ministration—and if required, in restoration and rehabilitation.

3. The Plan of Mercy Ministry. When the attainment plan and the bestowal plan had been formulated and proclaimed, alone and of himself, the Infinite Spirit projected and put in operation the tremendous and universal enterprise of mercy ministry.

ch28.s2.u1.k: The idea of appeasing an angry God with blood sacrifice is an affront to God.
ch28.s2.u1.p: For ages religion offered sacrifice, penance, and blood to buy the favor of God. The Urantia Book calls this idea a puerile and primitive philosophy and firmly rejects it. God is not divided into a personality of justice and another of mercy, so no mediator is needed between the two. The single sentence that God as a father transcends God as a judge sets the direction of the whole doctrine of salvation.

text: The barbarous idea of appeasing an angry God, of propitiating an offended Lord, of winning the favor of Deity through sacrifices and penance and even by the shedding of blood, represents a religion wholly puerile and primitive, a philosophy unworthy of an enlightened age of science and truth. … It is an affront to God to believe, hold, or teach that innocent blood must be shed in order to win his favor or to divert the fictitious divine wrath.

The affectionate heavenly Father, whose spirit indwells his children on earth, is not a divided personality—one of justice and one of mercy—neither does it require a mediator to secure the Father's favor or forgiveness. Divine righteousness is not dominated by strict retributive justice; God as a father transcends God as a judge.

ch28.s2.u2.k: The bestowals of the Sons do not change the Father's attitude; they reveal the Father's nature.
ch28.s2.u2.p: The notion that the Son came to turn the Father's heart is widespread. But the Father's love has been unchanging from the first, so there is nothing to change. A Creator Son condescends to take upon himself the form and experiences of his creatures, and in so doing he reveals the Father's loving nature and beneficent authority. A bestowal does not persuade the Father; it reveals him.

text: The finite understanding and creature appreciation of the Father's primacy is concerned in the adventure of a Creator Son when he condescends to take upon himself the form and experiences of his creatures. These primary Paradise Sons are the real revealers of the Father's loving nature and beneficent authority, the same Father who, in association with the Son and the Spirit, is the universal head of all power, personality, and government throughout all the universal realms.

ch28.s2.u3.k: Jesus did not die to atone for mankind's guilt or to appease the wrath of God.
ch28.s2.u3.p: The tradition of reading the cross as an offering of atonement and appeasement is deep and old. The Urantia Book plainly says that Jesus did not die to ransom man from apostate rulers, nor as a sacrifice to pay a debt mankind owed to God. Yet it does not erase the meaning of the cross; it notes that Urantia has become known among neighboring worlds as the World of the Cross. The cross did not change God's heart; it disclosed most deeply the love that was already there.

text: Jesus did not die to ransom man from the clutch of the apostate rulers and fallen princes of the spheres. … Neither was the Master's death on the cross a sacrifice which consisted in an effort to pay God a debt which the race of mankind had come to owe him.
It is a fact that Urantia has become known among other neighboring inhabited planets as the "World of the Cross."

ch28.s3.u1.k: Salvation is the Father's gift; accepted by faith, it makes one a son of God.
ch28.s3.u1.p: Jesus taught that salvation is a gift given by the Father and revealed by his Sons. What man must do is accept that gift by faith. By faith one is justified, by faith saved, and by the same faith one walks the endless path of perfection. Salvation is not an achievement of man but a gift freely given by the Father.

text: "Salvation is the gift of the Father and is revealed by his Sons. Acceptance by faith on your part makes you a partaker of the divine nature, a son or a daughter of God. By faith you are justified; by faith are you saved; and by this same faith are you eternally advanced in the way of progressive and divine perfection.

ch28.s3.u2.k: A righteous life is not the condition of salvation but the natural fruit of sonship already received.
ch28.s3.u2.p: Salvation is the gift of God, and righteousness is the natural fruit of the life that has received it. This does not make morality light; it puts things in the right order. We do not live righteously in order to be saved; we live righteously because we have been saved. One who has realized that he is a child of God finds it hard to live with the desire to sin. So kingdom believers do good not by compulsion but out of the joy of sonship.

text: Salvation is the gift of God, and righteousness is the natural fruit of the spirit-born life of sonship in the kingdom. You are not to be saved because you live a righteous life; rather is it that you live a righteous life because you have already been saved, have recognized sonship as the gift of God and service in the kingdom as the supreme delight of life on earth. … Realization of sonship is incompatible with the desire to sin.

ch28.s3.u3.k: Jesus abolished sacrifice and atonement and set the God-man relation on a parent-child basis.
ch28.s3.u3.p: Beneath the system of sacrifice lay a fictitious guilt, a sense of being abandoned alone in the universe. Jesus tore that foundation away by declaring that man is a child of God. Just as a child in a family pays no price to be loved, so no such ceremonies are needed in our relation with God. The Father looks not at a child's actual merit but at its motive and intent.

text: Jesus swept away all of the ceremonials of sacrifice and atonement. He destroyed the basis of all this fictitious guilt and sense of isolation in the universe by declaring that man is a child of God; the creature-Creator relationship was placed on a child-parent basis. God becomes a loving Father to his mortal sons and daughters.

God the Father deals with man his child on the basis, not of actual virtue or worthiness, but in recognition of the child's motivation—the creature purpose and intent. The relationship is one of parent-child association and is actuated by divine love.

ch28.s3.u4.k: Mortals become faith sons of God by accepting sonship through faith.
ch28.s3.u4.p: Sonship with God begins not as something inborn by nature but as a status received by faith. When a person accepts that status in faith, he is already a son of grace and mercy. To this are added the facts that a Creator Son has become our elder brother and that the spirit of the Son has been poured out on all. Salvation is not a distant reward but a place in the family enjoyed now.

text: All evolutionary worlds of mortal habitation harbor these faith sons of God, sons of grace and mercy, mortal beings belonging to the divine family and accordingly called the sons of God. Urantia mortals are entitled to regard themselves as being the sons of God because:
1. You are sons of spiritual promise, faith sons; you have accepted the status of sonship. You believe in the reality of your sonship, and thus does your sonship with God become eternally real.

2. A Creator Son of God became one of you; he is your elder brother in fact; and if in spirit you become truly related brothers of Christ, the victorious Michael, then in spirit must you also be sons of that Father which you have in common—even the Universal Father of all.

3. You are sons because the spirit of a Son has been poured out upon you, has been freely and certainly bestowed upon all Urantia races. This spirit ever draws you toward the divine Son, who is its source, and toward the Paradise Father, who is the source of that divine Son.

ch28.s4: The Salvation of Forgiveness and Love
ch28.s4.u1.k: God's forgiveness need not be sought, only received as restored loyalty.
ch28.s4.u1.p: Ancient man could feel God's favor only by offering sacrifice. Modern man needs a new way of becoming conscious of salvation. The Urantia Book explains forgiveness as the renewal of loyalty relations with God. Because God is always ready to forgive, our part is not to extract forgiveness by effort but to realize and receive the restoration.

text: Ancient man only attained consciousness of favor with God through sacrifice. Modern man must develop new techniques of achieving the self-consciousness of salvation.

The forgiveness of sin by Deity is the renewal of loyalty relations following a period of the human consciousness of the lapse of such relations as the consequence of conscious rebellion. The forgiveness does not have to be sought, only received as the consciousness of re-establishment of loyalty relations between the creature and the Creator.

ch28.s4.u2.k: The cross places God and man on a family basis and shows a love that destroys sin.
ch28.s4.u2.p: The central truth of the universe is not the justice of a king who seeks satisfaction in the sufferings of an offending subject, but the love of a father for his son. The cross shows this forever. Mercy sets guilt to one side, but love destroys the sin and its weakness altogether. Jesus' forgiveness is not condonation but salvation from condemnation, and salvation does not slight wrongs; it makes them right.

text: It forever places all relations between God and man upon the family basis. God is the Father; man is his son. Love, the love of a father for his son, becomes the central truth in the universe relations of Creator and creature—not the justice of a king which seeks satisfaction in the sufferings and punishment of the evil-doing subject.

The forgiveness of love utterly transcends the forgiveness of mercy. Mercy sets the guilt of evil-doing to one side; but love destroys forever the sin and all weakness resulting therefrom. … The forgiveness of Jesus is not condonation; it is salvation from condemnation. Salvation does not slight wrongs; it makes them right.

ch28.qs1: Have I ever felt I had to offer something to win God's love? Where did that feeling come from?
ch28.qs2: How does the order 'we live righteously because we are saved' change my moral striving?
ch28.qs3: How can I practice in my relationships the difference between forgiveness that covers sin and love that makes things right?
ch29.sum: The Christology of the Urantia Book sees Jesus as Michael, the Creator Son of our local universe. Through seven bestowals he became a wise and sympathetic sovereign, and in the seventh and final bestowal he took human form on Urantia. He was not God in association with man but God incarnate in man, God and man from first to last. He was a true man who labored, grew weary, was tested, and died; and at the same time he was the revelation of the Father, who could say that he who had seen him had seen the Father. This chapter considers in turn Michael's bestowals, the oneness of divinity and humanity, the life and character that revealed the Father, and the religion of Jesus as distinct from a religion about Jesus. The aim of Christology is not to leave Jesus only as an object of worship but to lead us to believe as he believed and to follow him.
ch29.s1.u1.k: A Creator Son's bestowals make him a wise, sympathetic, and understanding sovereign.
ch29.s1.u1.p: The life of Jesus is not a sudden exception but the final stage of a path all Creator Sons walk. A Creator Son is endowed with justice and righteousness, yet the Ancients of Days will not certify him as universe sovereign until he has lived as a creature in the creature's own environment; the ruler stands where the ruled stand. Christology begins here: our sovereign is one who knows our life from within.

text: But such endowments of justice and righteousness will not suffice in the estimate of the Ancients of Days. These triune rulers of the superuniverses will never certify a Creator Son as Universe Sovereign until he has really acquired the viewpoint of his own creatures by actual experience in the environment of their existence and as these very creatures themselves.

ch29.s1.u2.k: Through seven bestowals Michael qualified to rule as supreme representative of the Trinity.
ch29.s1.u2.p: A Creator Son may rule his universe in his own right from the start. But Michael was not content with that; he sought to complete the experience of creature understanding by living seven times as various orders of creatures. His life on Urantia was the last of these bestowals. The meaning of this bestowal career is that sovereignty earned by experience inspires a deeper trust than sovereignty held by right.

text: Michael, therefore, had a double purpose in the making of these seven bestowals upon the various orders of his universe creatures: First, he was completing the required experience in creature understanding which is demanded of all Creator Sons before they assume complete sovereignty. At any time a Creator Son may rule his universe in his own right, but he can rule as the supreme representative of the Paradise Trinity only after passing through the seven universe-creature bestowals.

ch29.s1.u3.k: In the Urantia bestowal Michael laid aside all superhuman help and depended wholly on the Father.
ch29.s1.u3.p: This passage is part of the counsel Michael received before his bestowal. Just as his creatures depend on him, he now had to depend wholly on his Paradise Father. The Creator of a universe chose to live as a man trusting the Father. So the faith Jesus asks of us is not a command handed down from above; it is a road he walked first.

text: "In entering upon the Urantia bestowal, you have voluntarily divested yourself of all extraplanetary support and special assistance such as might be rendered by any creature of your own creation. As your created sons of Nebadon are wholly dependent upon you for safe conduct throughout their universe careers, so now must you become wholly and unreservedly dependent upon your Paradise Father for safe conduct throughout the unrevealed vicissitudes of your ensuing mortal career.

ch29.s2.u1.k: In Jesus, God and man were joined in one unified personality.
ch29.s2.u1.p: The long debate of Christology has been how divinity and humanity relate in Jesus. The Jews of his day pictured the Messiah as perfected human, as superhuman, even as divine, but never conceived of the two natures joined in one personality. That was revealed only in Jesus. The Urantia Book teaches that God and man can coexist in a unified personality, and that the present status of Christ Michael demonstrates it.

text: There was one feature of the bestowal of Michael which was utterly foreign to the Jewish conception of the Messiah, and that was the union of the two natures, the human and the divine. The Jews had variously conceived of the Messiah as perfected human, superhuman, and even as divine, but they never entertained the concept of the union of the human and the divine.

On attained experiential levels all personality orders or values are associable and even cocreational. Even God and man can coexist in a unified personality, as is so exquisitely demonstrated in the present status of Christ Michael—Son of Man and Son of God.

ch29.s2.u2.k: Jesus was a true man of flesh and blood who labored, grew weary, was tested, and died.
ch29.s2.u2.p: Emphasis on his divinity can make Jesus' humanity seem like an outer garment. The text corrects that tendency. He hungered, thirsted, and slept, and he passed through the full range of human feelings. That the Creator Son was literally made flesh and dwelt as a man of the realm tells us his human experience was no appearance but reality.

text: It is literally true that the creative Word—the Creator Son—of the Universal Father was "made flesh and dwelt as a man of the realm on Urantia." He labored, grew weary, rested, and slept. He hungered and satisfied such cravings with food; he thirsted and quenched his thirst with water. He experienced the full gamut of human feelings and emotions; he was "in all things tested, even as you are," and he suffered and died.

ch29.s2.u3.k: Consciousness of divinity grew gradually in Jesus' mind until his baptism.
ch29.s2.u3.p: Jesus did not grow up as a child who knew everything from the start. His awareness of his divine nature and prehuman existence grew gradually and was completed at his baptism. After that he seems to have had the power to limit his human consciousness of his divinity. His life can be an example to us precisely because he truly bore the limits of a man.

text: Consciousness of divinity was a gradual growth in the mind of Jesus up to the occasion of his baptism. After he became fully self-conscious of his divine nature, prehuman existence, and universe prerogatives, he seems to have possessed the power of variously limiting his human consciousness of his divinity.

ch29.s3: A Life That Revealed the Father
ch29.s3.u1.k: To see Jesus, more than to hear his words, is the way to know the Father.
ch29.s3.u1.p: Jesus taught little doctrine about the Father; that God is spirit and is a Father to his creatures was almost all. Instead he showed the Father by his life. So he never said that whoever heard him had heard God, but that whoever had seen him had seen the Father. The center of revelation is not a sentence but a person.

text: Although Jesus revealed the true nature of the heavenly Father in his earth life, he taught little about him. In fact, he taught only two things: that God in himself is spirit, and that, in all matters of relationship with his creatures, he is a Father.

But mark you! never did Jesus say, "Whoso has heard me has heard God." But he did say, "He who has seen me has seen the Father." To hear Jesus' teaching is not equivalent to knowing God, but to see Jesus is an experience which in itself is a revelation of the Father to the soul.

ch29.s3.u2.k: Jesus' character, sincere and original, showed love and mercy in place of fear.
ch29.s3.u2.p: What revealed the Father was not so much Jesus' miracles as his character. He was without affectation, lived as he taught, and was the truth itself. Unbound by tradition, he still did not discard the gems of older truth. The newest thing in his teaching was its emphasis on love and mercy in place of fear and sacrifice. In that character we see what God is like.

text: The unfailing kindness of Jesus touched the hearts of men, but his stalwart strength of character amazed his followers. He was truly sincere; there was nothing of the hypocrite in him. He was free from affectation; he was always so refreshingly genuine. He never stooped to pretense, and he never resorted to shamming. He lived the truth, even as he taught it. He was the truth.

Jesus' originality was unstifled. He was not bound by tradition or handicapped by enslavement to narrow conventionality. … But his superb originality did not cause him to overlook the gems of truth in the teachings of his predecessors and contemporaries. And the most original of his teachings was the emphasis of love and mercy in the place of fear and sacrifice.

ch29.s3.u3.k: Jesus' faith was not traditional or intellectual but a personal trust pure as a child's.
ch29.s3.u3.p: Before he was an object of faith, Jesus was a man of faith. He went through all the ups and downs of life, yet never doubted God's watchcare. His faith was not an inherited tradition or a conclusion of the intellect but an insight born of communion with his indwelling Adjuster. In a mature intellect the trust of a child reigned. It was childlike, but never childish.

text: JESUS enjoyed a sublime and wholehearted faith in God. He experienced the ordinary ups and downs of mortal existence, but he never religiously doubted the certainty of God's watchcare and guidance. His faith was the outgrowth of the insight born of the activity of the divine presence, his indwelling Adjuster. His faith was neither traditional nor merely intellectual; it was wholly personal and purely spiritual.

The faith of Jesus attained the purity of a child's trust. … In this giant intellect of the full-grown man the faith of the child reigned supreme in all matters relating to the religious consciousness. … Notwithstanding that Jesus' faith was childlike, it was in no sense childish.

ch29.s4.u1.k: Jesus asks us not to believe in him but to believe with him, and to follow him.
ch29.s4.u1.p: The final question of Christology shifts from "Who is Jesus?" to "How shall we follow him?" Rather than demanding belief in himself, Jesus invites us to believe what he believed, and as he believed. To follow him is to share his faith and enter into his spirit of unselfish service for others. The most valuable knowledge is to know how Jesus lived.

text: Jesus does not require his disciples to believe in him but rather to believe with him, believe in the reality of the love of God and in full confidence accept the security of the assurance of sonship with the heavenly Father. … Jesus most touchingly challenged his followers, not only to believe what he believed, but also to believe as he believed. This is the full significance of his one supreme requirement, "Follow me."

To "follow Jesus" means to personally share his religious faith and to enter into the spirit of the Master's life of unselfish service for man. … Of all human knowledge, that which is of greatest value is to know the religious life of Jesus and how he lived it.

ch29.s4.u2.k: Jesus founded a religion of personal experience; later followers founded a religion of worshiping Jesus.
ch29.s4.u2.p: The religion of Jesus and the religion about Jesus are not the same. One is the personal experience of doing God's will and serving one's brothers; the other is a community of faith that worships the glorified Christ. Both were latent in his divine-human life. Rather than setting them against each other, the text regrets that no unified religion arose honoring both his human and his divine natures.

text: Jesus founded the religion of personal experience in doing the will of God and serving the human brotherhood; Paul founded a religion in which the glorified Jesus became the object of worship and the brotherhood consisted of fellow believers in the divine Christ.

ch29.s4.u3.k: The cross is not an offering to appease wrath but a symbol of the good giving themselves for the evil.
ch29.s4.u3.p: Jesus' death must be read in the same light as his life. The cross is not a sign of an innocent Son offered to an angry God in place of sinners. It is the symbol of holy service that gives one's life to the very end for the welfare and salvation of others. So the cross is not a sign of fear but the everlasting symbol of the good saving the evil by the devotion of love.

text: The cross is that high symbol of sacred service, the devotion of one's life to the welfare and salvation of one's fellows. The cross is not the symbol of the sacrifice of the innocent Son of God in the place of guilty sinners and in order to appease the wrath of an offended God, but it does stand forever, on earth and throughout a vast universe, as a sacred symbol of the good bestowing themselves upon the evil and thereby saving them by this very devotion of love.

ch29.qs1: What comfort does it give my own growth in faith that Jesus' awareness of his divinity grew gradually and that he depended wholly on the Father?
ch29.qs2: How does the difference between believing in Jesus and believing with Jesus show up in my religious life?
ch29.qs3: Which trait of Jesus' character do I most want to share today, and what can I do toward it?
ch30.sub: The Inner Experience Ruled by the Father's Will
ch30.sum: The center of the gospel Jesus preached was the kingdom of heaven. Yet that kingdom is not a visible nation or institution but a spiritual relationship found wherever the spirit of God teaches and leads the soul of man. In it there is no high and mighty king, but a divine family of the Father and his sons. One enters the kingdom by faith, recognizing God's sovereignty, believing in sonship, and making the Father's will one's own. The religion of the kingdom is personal, but its fruits spread through society as brotherly love and unselfish service. This chapter considers in turn the nature of the kingdom, the way of entrance, its personal and social dimensions and growth, and the relation between the kingdom and the church. The kingdom is an experience that begins small as a mustard seed and grows all the way to Paradise, and its first home is always a single human heart.
ch30.s1.u1.k: The kingdom of heaven is not visible; it is wherever God's spirit leads the soul of man.
ch30.s1.u1.p: The Jews of Jesus' day awaited the kingdom of God as a political event, the restoration of David's realm. Jesus turned that expectation around. The kingdom is not a material thing to be found here or there; it is already among us, and its power lies not in armies or riches but in the spirit that teaches minds and rules hearts. Its marks are righteousness, peace, and joy.

text: "Be not deceived by those who come saying here is the kingdom or there is the kingdom, for my Father's kingdom concerns not things visible and material. And this kingdom is even now among you, for where the spirit of God teaches and leads the soul of man, there in reality is the kingdom of heaven. And this kingdom of God is righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.

"The power of this kingdom shall consist, not in the strength of armies nor in the might of riches, but rather in the glory of the divine spirit that shall come to teach the minds and rule the hearts of the reborn citizens of this heavenly kingdom, the sons of God.

ch30.s1.u2.k: The kingdom consists in recognizing God's sovereignty, believing in sonship, and desiring to do God's will.
ch30.s1.u2.p: Jesus summed up the kingdom in three essentials: recognizing that God is sovereign, believing that we are his sons, and having faith in the power of the supreme desire to do his will. Since God is spirit, this kingdom is spiritual. It is neither a material thing nor a system of knowledge; it is a living relationship between God and man.

text: John asked Jesus, "Master, what is the kingdom of heaven?" And Jesus answered: "The kingdom of heaven consists in these three essentials: first, recognition of the fact of the sovereignty of God; second, belief in the truth of sonship with God; and third, faith in the effectiveness of the supreme human desire to do the will of God—to be like God.

The kingdom of heaven, the divine government, is founded on the fact of divine sovereignty—God is spirit. Since God is spirit, this kingdom is spiritual. The kingdom of heaven is neither material nor merely intellectual; it is a spiritual relationship between God and man.

ch30.s1.u3.k: The kingdom Jesus proclaimed has no mighty king; it is a divine family of the Father and his sons.
ch30.s1.u3.p: "Kingdom" was a word Jesus inherited, but what he put into it was not the relation of king and subject. It is not a realm ruled by a high and mighty king but a divine family of a Father and his children. So he asks us to stop fearing God as a king or serving him as a master, and instead to reverence him as Creator and love him as Father. As faith matures, this love deepens into worship.

text: "In the kingdom of heaven, which I have come to declare, there is no high and mighty king; this kingdom is a divine family. … Cease, then, to fear God as a king or serve him as a master; learn to reverence him as the Creator; honor him as the Father of your spirit youth; love him as a merciful defender; and ultimately worship him as the loving and all-wise Father of your more mature spiritual realization and appreciation.

ch30.s2.u1.k: When the Father's will becomes truly one's own will, one is truly in the kingdom.
ch30.s2.u1.p: One who keeps God's will as an outward law differs from one who has made that will his own. Jesus says that while the Father's will remains a law, one is hardly in the kingdom. When that will truly becomes one's own, one is in very truth in the kingdom. The kingdom becomes an established experience within a person when that will becomes the desire of the heart.

text: Verily, verily, I say to you, when the Father's will is your law, you are hardly in the kingdom. But when the Father's will becomes truly your will, then are you in very truth in the kingdom because the kingdom has thereby become an established experience in you.

ch30.s2.u2.k: Unless one is born of the spirit, one cannot enter the kingdom of God.
ch30.s2.u2.p: In his conversation with Nicodemus, Jesus called the door into the kingdom being born from above. This is not reforming oneself by moral effort but the spirit raising new life within a person. As we know the wind by the rustle of the leaves though we cannot see it, so it is with everyone born of the spirit. The kingdom begins, before any human resolve, with the birth of the spirit.

text: Jesus said: "Nevertheless, I declare to you, except a man be born of the spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. … But you should not marvel that I said you must be born from above. When the wind blows, you hear the rustle of the leaves, but you do not see the wind—whence it comes or whither it goes—and so it is with everyone born of the spirit.

ch30.s2.u3.k: Faith is the price of entering God's family, and the forgiven one loves and forgives his neighbor.
ch30.s2.u3.p: Even after entering the door by faith, the righteousness of the kingdom must grow. Jesus explained the way through the experience of forgiveness. God's forgiveness is actually experienced in the measure that one forgives one's fellows, and one cannot truly forgive without loving one's neighbor as oneself. From that love moral conduct flows naturally. Righteousness is not strained effort but the fruit of love.

text: It is in the consideration of the technique of receiving God's forgiveness that the attainment of the righteousness of the kingdom is revealed. Faith is the price you pay for entrance into the family of God; but forgiveness is the act of God which accepts your faith as the price of admission.
1. God's forgiveness is made actually available and is personally experienced by man just in so far as he forgives his fellows.
2. Man will not truly forgive his fellows unless he loves them as himself.
3. To thus love your neighbor as yourself is the highest ethics.
4. Moral conduct, true righteousness, becomes, then, the natural result of such love.

ch30.s3: Person, Society, and the Growth of the Kingdom
ch30.s3.u1.k: The religion of the kingdom is personal, but its fruits are familial and social.
ch30.s3.u1.p: Because the kingdom begins in the individual heart, Jesus always exalted the sacredness of the person above the community. Yet the experience does not stay shut up within the individual. A person grows in character through unselfish service and unfolds his moral nature in loving relations with others. So the love call of the kingdom breaks down the world's hate, and the believer's unselfish service carries light to those in darkness.

text: The religion of the kingdom is personal, individual; the fruits, the results, are familial, social. Jesus never failed to exalt the sacredness of the individual as contrasted with the community. But he also recognized that man develops his character by unselfish service; that he unfolds his moral nature in loving relations with his fellows.

The love call of the spiritual kingdom should prove to be the effective destroyer of the hate urge of the unbelieving and war-minded citizens of the earthly kingdoms. But these material-minded sons in darkness will never know of your spiritual light of truth unless you draw very near them with that unselfish social service which is the natural outgrowth of the bearing of the fruits of the spirit in the life experience of each individual believer.

ch30.s3.u2.k: The kingdom is an evolutionary experience that begins on earth and grows all the way to Paradise.
ch30.s3.u2.p: The kingdom does not drop from heaven complete in a single moment. Jesus explained that it is an experience beginning on this earth and advancing through successive life stations to Paradise. The parable of the mustard seed pictures this. As the least of seeds becomes a tree where birds can rest, the small faith within one person at last becomes shade where many find rest.

text: Very plainly Jesus explained that the kingdom of heaven was an evolutionary experience, beginning here on earth and progressing up through successive life stations to Paradise.

After the people had asked a few questions, Jesus spoke another parable: "The kingdom of heaven is like a grain of mustard seed which a man sowed in his field. Now a mustard seed is the least of seeds, but when it is full grown, it becomes the greatest of all herbs and is like a tree so that the birds of heaven are able to come and rest in the branches thereof."

ch30.s3.u3.k: The world has never seriously tried the ideals of the kingdom, but each must first establish it in his own soul.
ch30.s3.u3.p: Looking at history, the progress of the kingdom seems slow. Yet the text says the world has never seriously tried out Jesus' ideals of the kingdom. Slow progress means not that the ideals have failed but that they have not yet been tried. The more important warning is not to make the mistake of waiting for the kingdom to appear in the world while failing to establish it in our own souls. The kingdom advances first within each person.

text: This world has never seriously or sincerely or honestly tried out these dynamic ideas and divine ideals of Jesus' doctrine of the kingdom of heaven. … Neither make the fatal mistake, in looking for the age manifestation of the kingdom, of failing to effect its establishment within your own souls.

ch30.s4.u1.k: The church could have been a natural social fruit of the kingdom, but it nearly replaced the kingdom concept.
ch30.s4.u1.p: It is natural and good for believers to gather in community. The problem was not the church's existence but its taking the place of the kingdom. To the Jews the kingdom was the community of Israel; to the gentiles it became the Christian church. But to Jesus the kingdom was the spiritual brotherhood of individuals who believed in the fatherhood of God and dedicated themselves to doing his will.

text: The church, as a social outgrowth of the kingdom, would have been wholly natural and even desirable. The evil of the church was not its existence, but rather that it almost completely supplanted the Jesus concept of the kingdom. Paul's institutionalized church became a virtual substitute for the kingdom of heaven which Jesus had proclaimed.

The kingdom, to the Jews, was the Israelite community; to the gentiles it became the Christian church. To Jesus the kingdom was the sum of those individuals who had confessed their faith in the fatherhood of God, thereby declaring their wholehearted dedication to the doing of the will of God, thus becoming members of the spiritual brotherhood of man.

ch30.s4.u2.k: The inner kingdom Jesus taught will yet be proclaimed again to every church, religion, nation, and person.
ch30.s4.u2.p: That the story about Jesus displaced Jesus' gospel of the kingdom is a painful chapter of history. Yet the text does not give up hope. The kingdom that exists in the believer's heart will yet be proclaimed to the Christian church and to every other religion, nation, and individual. That proclamation will be a return not to a visible church or the expectation of a second coming, but to the Father's will ruling in the believer's heart.

text: But doubt not, this same kingdom of heaven which the Master taught exists within the heart of the believer, will yet be proclaimed to this Christian church, even as to all other religions, races, and nations on earth—even to every individual.

Sooner or later another and greater John the Baptist is due to arise proclaiming "the kingdom of God is at hand"—meaning a return to the high spiritual concept of Jesus, who proclaimed that the kingdom is the will of his heavenly Father dominant and transcendent in the heart of the believer—and doing all this without in any way referring either to the visible church on earth or to the anticipated second coming of Christ.

ch30.qs1: In what areas does God's will still remain an outward law for me, and what would it take for it to become my own will?
ch30.qs2: How are the inner fruits of the kingdom I have experienced flowing out as service to my family and neighbors?
ch30.qs3: For me, how are belonging to a church or faith community and belonging to the kingdom of heaven alike, and how are they different?
ch31.sub: The New Teacher Who Leads into All Truth
ch31.sum: Before he departed, Jesus promised his followers that he would send another teacher, and at Pentecost the Spirit of Truth was poured out upon all flesh. This spirit is not the letter or law of truth but the conviction of living and growing truth, and it makes us conscious not of itself but of Michael the Son. The Spirit of Truth was given not only to the apostles but to all sincere believers, and from then on Thought Adjusters came to indwell every normal mind. This chapter considers in turn the promise of the new teacher, the nature of the Spirit of Truth, the meaning of Pentecost, and the mission and fruits of that spirit. If religion before Pentecost showed man seeking God, after Pentecost it also shows God seeking man. The Spirit of Truth makes the Jesus of history the living experience of believers today.
ch31.s1.u1.k: Jesus promised to send another teacher in his stead, the Spirit of Truth, after ascending to the Father.
ch31.s1.u1.p: The promise of the Spirit of Truth was there from early in Jesus' public life. He said that just as the Father's spirit indwells human minds, so after his work was done the Spirit of Truth would be poured out on all flesh, and that together these spirits would establish believers in the kingdom of spiritual understanding. After ascending to the Father, he kept that promise at Pentecost. His departure was not abandonment but a way of coming nearer.

text: The Father in heaven sends his spirit to indwell the minds of men, and when I shall have finished my work on earth, likewise shall the Spirit of Truth be poured out upon all flesh. And the spirit of my Father and the Spirit of Truth shall establish you in the coming kingdom of spiritual understanding and divine righteousness.

Jesus promised to do two things after he had ascended to the Father, and after all power in heaven and on earth had been placed in his hands. He promised, first, to send into the world, and in his stead, another teacher, the Spirit of Truth; and this he did on the day of Pentecost.

ch31.s1.u2.k: As Jesus had lived with his disciples, he would now live in them and lead them into all truth.
ch31.s1.u2.p: At the Last Supper Jesus promised his disciples, on the eve of parting, a new relationship. Until then he had been beside them; now he would be within them, one with their personal experience. As the Father had given him his spirit, so he would give them his. That spirit would guide and comfort and at last lead them into all truth. Presence beside them would become presence within them.

text: As I have lived with you in person, then shall I live in you; I shall be one with your personal experience in the spirit kingdom. … As my Father has given me of his spirit, so will I give you of my spirit. And this Spirit of Truth which I will bestow upon you shall guide and comfort you and shall eventually lead you into all truth.

ch31.s1.u3.k: The Spirit of Truth is poured out on all flesh, but becomes a well of living water only in those who receive him.
ch31.s1.u3.p: The gift is given to all, but receiving it is each person's choice. His spirit is poured out upon all flesh, but not everyone will receive it as the guide and counselor of the soul. Yet those who accept him as counselor of the soul are enlightened, cleansed, and comforted. The spirit becomes not a guest who calls now and then from outside but a spring welling up unceasingly within.

text: I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh, but all men will not choose to receive this new teacher as the guide and counselor of the soul. But as many as do receive him shall be enlightened, cleansed, and comforted. And this Spirit of Truth will become in them a well of living water springing up into eternal life.

ch31.s2: The Nature of the Spirit of Truth
ch31.s2.u1.k: The Spirit of Truth is not the letter or law of truth but the conviction of living and growing truth.
ch31.s2.u1.p: To think of the Spirit of Truth as a guarantee for doctrine is to miss its nature. This spirit is not a form of truth but the conviction of true meanings, the spirit of truth that is ever unfolding, adapting, and growing. So truth can be known, lived, and experienced, but never imprisoned in formulas or creeds. The moment truth is locked in a human framework it becomes dead theory. Living truth breathes only in experience.

text: The new helper which Jesus promised to send into the hearts of believers, to pour out upon all flesh, is the Spirit of Truth. This divine endowment is not the letter or law of truth, neither is it to function as the form or expression of truth. The new teacher is the conviction of truth, the consciousness and assurance of true meanings on real spirit levels. And this new teacher is the spirit of living and growing truth, expanding, unfolding, and adaptative truth.

You can know the truth, and you can live the truth; you can experience the growth of truth in the soul and enjoy the liberty of its enlightenment in the mind, but you cannot imprison truth in formulas, codes, creeds, or intellectual patterns of human conduct. When you undertake the human formulation of divine truth, it speedily dies.

ch31.s2.u2.k: The Spirit of Truth creates consciousness not of himself but of Michael the Son.
ch31.s2.u2.p: The proof of experiencing the Spirit of Truth is not an intense awareness of the spirit. This spirit does not display himself; he only deepens fellowship with Jesus. So if we would know whether we commune with the Spirit of Truth, we should ask not about mystical feelings but whether our relationship with Christ has grown. If the Adjuster is the presence of the Father, the Spirit of Truth is the presence of the Sons.

text: Do not make the mistake of expecting to become strongly intellectually conscious of the outpoured Spirit of Truth. The spirit never creates a consciousness of himself, only a consciousness of Michael, the Son. … The proof, therefore, of your fellowship with the Spirit of Truth is not to be found in your consciousness of this spirit but rather in your experience of enhanced fellowship with Michael.

The Adjuster is the presence of the Father; the Spirit of Truth, the presence of the Sons. These divine endowments are unified and co-ordinated on the lower levels of human spiritual experience by the ministry of the guardian seraphim.

ch31.s2.u3.k: The working of the Spirit of Truth depends on how fully man receives it.
ch31.s2.u3.p: The Spirit of Truth has been poured out on everyone, but its power depends on each person's capacity of receptivity. Prayer does not bring the spirit, yet it digs larger and deeper channels through which the divine bestowals may flow. Within a person the Father's Adjuster, the Son's Spirit of Truth, and the Universe Spirit's Holy Spirit work together, and these three gifts are unified as the ministry of the Supreme. God dwells in man through a threefold gift.

text: Prayer did not bring the spirit on the day of Pentecost, but it did have much to do with determining the capacity of receptivity which characterized the individual believers. Prayer does not move the divine heart to liberality of bestowal, but it does so often dig out larger and deeper channels wherein the divine bestowals may flow to the hearts and souls of those who thus remember to maintain unbroken communion with their Maker through sincere prayer and true worship.

Divinity functions in mortal personality as the Adjuster gift of the Father, as the Spirit of Truth of the Son, and as the Holy Spirit of the Universe Spirit, while these three supermortal endowments are unified in human experiential evolution as the ministry of the Supreme.

ch31.s3.u1.k: At Pentecost the praying believers became aware of a new presence and of spiritual joy and confidence.
ch31.s3.u1.p: The event of Pentecost began not with dramatic signs but with inner change. The one hundred and twenty believers sensed a strange presence in the room, and at once became conscious of deep joy, security, and confidence. Peter recognized it as the Spirit of Truth the Master had promised. The coming of the spirit turned those who had hidden in fear into witnesses.

text: ABOUT one o'clock, as the one hundred and twenty believers were engaged in prayer, they all became aware of a strange presence in the room. At the same time these disciples all became conscious of a new and profound sense of spiritual joy, security, and confidence.

Peter stood up and declared that this must be the coming of the Spirit of Truth which the Master had promised them and proposed that they go to the temple and begin the proclamation of the good news committed to their hands. And they did just what Peter suggested.

ch31.s3.u2.k: The Spirit of Truth was given to all sincere believers, and now God is seen seeking man.
ch31.s3.u2.p: The gift of Pentecost was not a privilege of the apostles alone. Every man and woman in the upper room received the spirit, as did honest hearts throughout the world. So true religion was freed from the custody of priests and sacred classes and came to find expression in individual souls. More remarkable still is the change of direction: to a religion of man seeking God was added God seeking man and dwelling within him.

text: Do not overlook the fact that the Spirit of Truth was bestowed upon all sincere believers; this gift of the spirit did not come only to the apostles. The one hundred and twenty men and women assembled in the upper chamber all received the new teacher, as did all the honest of heart throughout the whole world. … At last, true religion is delivered from the custody of priests and all sacred classes and finds its real manifestation in the individual souls of men.

Up to Pentecost, religion had revealed only man seeking for God; since Pentecost, man is still searching for God, but there shines out over the world the spectacle of God also seeking for man and sending his spirit to dwell within him when he has found him.

ch31.s3.u3.k: After the Spirit of Truth was poured out, Thought Adjusters came to indwell all normal will creatures.
ch31.s3.u3.p: The bestowal of the Spirit of Truth also opened the way for another divine gift. When a bestowal Son's mission is completed and the Spirit of Truth is poured out on all, Adjusters flock to that world to indwell every normal mind. Then the Adjuster truly becomes the kingdom of heaven within you. The Father's spirit now dwells not in a favored few but in every normal mind.

text: No matter what the previous status of the inhabitants of a world, subsequent to the bestowal of a divine Son and after the bestowal of the Spirit of Truth upon all humans, the Adjusters flock to such a world to indwell the minds of all normal will creatures. Following the completion of the mission of a Paradise bestowal Son, these Monitors truly become the "kingdom of heaven within you."

ch31.s4: The Mission and Fruits of the Spirit of Truth
ch31.s4.u1.k: The Spirit of Truth fosters truth, removes the believer's loneliness, and makes Jesus' life live anew.
ch31.s4.u1.p: The mission of the Spirit of Truth has several strands. First it fosters truth, for understanding truth is the highest liberty a person can know. Next it removes the orphaned loneliness believers would feel after Jesus' departure. It also helps them recall his words, reinterpret his life, and live afresh in each generation of believers the life he lived in the flesh.

text: The first mission of this spirit is, of course, to foster and personalize truth, for it is the comprehension of truth that constitutes the highest form of human liberty. Next, it is the purpose of this spirit to destroy the believer's feeling of orphanhood.
The spirit also came to help men recall and understand the words of the Master as well as to illuminate and reinterpret his life on earth.

Next, the Spirit of Truth came to help the believer to witness to the realities of Jesus' teachings and his life as he lived it in the flesh, and as he now again lives it anew and afresh in the individual believer of each passing generation of the spirit-filled sons of God.

Thus it appears that the Spirit of Truth comes really to lead all believers into all truth, into the expanding knowledge of the experience of the living and growing spiritual consciousness of the reality of eternal and ascending sonship with God.

ch31.s4.u2.k: The Spirit of Truth purifies the heart and is a force leading man upward and urging him onward.
ch31.s4.u2.p: The charge that religion is an opiate that numbs people does not fit the religion of Jesus. On the cross he refused even the drug that would have dulled his pain, and his spirit does not lull people to sleep but raises them up. The Spirit of Truth turns selfishness into selflessness and gathers life's purpose around God's will and the welfare of others. Its joy strengthens body, mind, and soul alike.

text: The coming of the Spirit of Truth purifies the human heart and leads the recipient to formulate a life purpose single to the will of God and the welfare of men. The material spirit of selfishness has been swallowed up in this new spiritual bestowal of selflessness. … The joy of this outpoured spirit, when it is consciously experienced in human life, is a tonic for health, a stimulus for mind, and an unfailing energy for the soul.

If religion is an opiate to the people, it is not the religion of Jesus. On the cross he refused to drink the deadening drug, and his spirit, poured out upon all flesh, is a mighty world influence which leads man upward and urges him onward.

ch31.s4.u3.k: In the Spirit of Truth, the golden rule becomes a call to love others as Jesus loved us.
ch31.s4.u3.p: The same golden rule means different things depending on the spirit in which it is read. Read only by the letter it is a rule of conduct; in the Spirit of Truth it becomes a living reality. When those led by the Spirit of Truth grasp its true meaning, they overflow with the assurance of citizenship in a friendly universe, and find satisfaction only in loving others as Jesus loved us.

text: But the highest realization and the truest interpretation of the golden rule consists in the consciousness of the spirit of the truth of the enduring and living reality of such a divine declaration. … And when such spirit-led mortals realize the true meaning of this golden rule, they are filled to overflowing with the assurance of citizenship in a friendly universe, and their ideals of spirit reality are satisfied only when they love their fellows as Jesus loved us all, and that is the reality of the realization of the love of God.

ch31.qs1: If I measure fellowship with the Spirit of Truth not by mystical feelings but by a deepened relationship with Jesus, where does my faith stand now?
ch31.qs2: Are there places where I am imprisoning truth in formulas or creeds and turning it into dead truth?
ch31.qs3: What comfort and what responsibility does the Pentecostal message of a God who seeks man bring me today?
